glosses: to bribe (to give a bribe to)
zjednywać sobie kogo, dając mu coś wartościowego
Something (usually money) given in exchange for influence or as an inducement to breaking the law.

examples.text:
c. 1613-1625, Henry Hobart, Yardly v. Ellill
Undue reward for anything against justice is a bribe.
The bribes I took did not influence me to become evil. I was evil from the beginning and the bribes were merely a bonus

glosses: The act of offering or paying such a payment: an act of bribery.
That which seduces; seduction; allurement.

examples.text: Not the bribes of sordid wealth can seduce to leave these everblooming sweets.
Remy, this was a bribe! Our whole marriage has been nothing but a series of bribes!

glosses: To give a bribe to; specifically, to ask a person to do something against their original will, in exchange for some type of reward or relief from potential trouble.

examples.text: She was accused of trying to bribe the jury into making false statements.

October 23, 1848, Frederick William Robertson, an address delivered at the Opening of The Working Men's Institute
Neither is he worthy who bribes a man to vote against his conscience.

glosses: To gain by a bribe; to induce as by a bribe.

examples.text: to bribe somebody's compliance

glosses: Gâter, altérer, changer en mal.
